column1: # BirdView's own occurrence status, derived from GBIF (product.scopeIsRecurringAvifauna, decisions.scopeFromRecurrence).
# Generated by cmd/birdview-status. Not a copy of anything published.
# name<TAB>status<TAB>region<TAB>episodes<TAB>years<TAB>records<TAB>commonest region<TAB>its records there<TAB>all bird records there<TAB>last seen
# The last three columns are where the species makes up the biggest SHARE of
# what is recorded, which is not where it has the most records: California has
# 35x the Sharp-shinned Hawk records of Yukon and 118x the birdwatching, so the
# hawk is 1 record in 250 there against 1 in 835 in California. Dividing by the
# region's own total cancels out how hard anyone was looking. Both numbers are
# written rather than the ratio, so a share resting on nine records says so.
# Status is recurrence, not abundance: a species is established where its
# records fall in repeated episodes across years, however few they are.
# Sources: EOD - eBird Observation Dataset, doi:10.15468/aomfnb, and the
# iNaturalist research-grade dataset. Both CC BY 4.0.
# Corpus ends 2026-02-19. A species last recorded before 2001-02-19 is historical,
# not present: GBIF carries museum specimens under their collection dates,
# and Passenger Pigeon recurs across a century of them.
# `last seen` is the most recent date in the region column, or - where no
# date was measured. It is what makes a historical verdict checkable rather
# than asserted, so a page can say WHEN (product.undrawnSpeciesAnswer).
